Simultaneously supporting dual-arm coordination and high-degree-of-freedom fine manipulation with dexterous hands — an end-to-end VLA model.  

Previous mainstream VLA systems either focused on low-degree-of-freedom gripper control for dual arms or specialized in high-degree-of-freedom dexterous hand operations for a single arm, failing to address the dual requirements of dual-arm coordination and fine finger movements. For example, tasks like piston insertion require precise dual-arm coordination, while unscrewing bottle caps or fine object grasping rely on multi-finger flexible control. Such tasks have long lacked a unified VLA solution.  

Recently, the first open-source VLA model natively designed for dual-arm, dual-high-degree-of-freedom (36 degrees of freedom) dexterous manipulation, Dexora, broke the morphological barriers of previous VLAs, offering a new paradigm for the deployment of general-purpose dexterous robots.  

Hardware and Teleoperation: A Dexterous Data Foundation for Virtual-Real Collaboration  

The core prerequisite for high-degree-of-freedom dexterous manipulation is precise and scalable data collection. Dexora abandons single teleoperation solutions, adopting a hybrid "exoskeleton + VR" teleoperation system that simultaneously drives physical robots and MuJoCo digital twins, addressing the precision and scalability challenges of data collection at their root.  

▲ Schematic of Dex hardware and hybrid teleoperation system © [Deep Blue Embodied Intelligence] Compilation  

On the hardware level, Dexora is equipped with two 6-degree-of-freedom AIRBOT robotic arms and a pair of 12-degree-of-freedom XHAN

Soporta simultáneamente la coordinación de dos brazos y la operación de alta libertad de dos manos diestras — Modelo VLA de extremo a extremo  
Los sistemas VLA convencionales anteriores se centraban en el control de pinzas de baja libertad para dos brazos, o se especializaban en la operación de manos diestras de alta libertad para un solo brazo, sin poder satisfacer la doble demanda de coordinación de dos brazos y movimientos finos de los dedos. Por ejemplo, la inserción de un pistón requiere una coordinación precisa de ambos brazos, mientras que girar una tapa de botella o recoger objetos pequeños depende de la regulación flexible de múltiples dedos. Este tipo de tareas carecía durante mucho tiempo de una solución VLA unificada.
